result.title: TransArt3D: From Two States to Articulated 3D Reconstruction with Video Transition Priors
result.summary: Reconstructing interactable articulated assets from a few images is key to robotics and simulation, yet highly underconstrained. Existing optimization-based methods fit an articulated asset under a static 3D prior that scores each state independently, so per-state reconstruction errors leak into the estimated moving part and joint as false motion. Video diffusion models capture how objects move between states, but only implicitly in 2D. To this end, we present TransArt3D, an optimization-based framework that reconstructs an articulated 3D asset from two endpoint images by translating this video transition prior into explicit part structure and joint kinematics. It first lifts frames generated between the endpoints with a transition-coupled 3D consensus that applies the static 3D prior jointly across frames, stabilizing unchanging regions and initializing the parts and joint. A rectified-flow kinematic refinement then lets the video prior supervise a 3D motion field over the whole transition, while part assignment and a shared joint constrain the field throughout optimization, keeping per-state errors out of the articulation. Finally, a motion-aware canonical appearance fusion uses the recovered articulation to map both endpoint images onto one canonical surface, texturing regions that only one state reveals. On PartNet-Mobility, TransArt3D outperforms methods given the same two endpoints in geometry and joint accuracy, and surpasses methods given six observed states in articulated-state geometry, joint localization and appearance.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 TransArt3D，从两张端点图像重建带关节的可交互 3D 资产，把视频扩散的过渡先验转成显式部件结构与关节运动学，并用其监督整段过渡上的 3D 运动场。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用整段过渡约束运动场、把不变区域与运动部件分离，避免单状态误差渗入结构」的思路，可能为 LVR 中区分任务不变内容与随推理推进的状态变化提供概念线索，但属 3D 资产重建，可供核查迁移价值。
